newsitem.title: USA: Campbell had record Q1 on strong soup sales.
newsitem.headline: Campbell had record Q1 on strong soup sales.

text.p: Campbell Soup Co Wednesday reported record sales and earnings for its first quarter ended October 27, saying the results were driven by the powerful combination of 11 percent higher sales in worldwide wet soup along with strong gains in productivity.
"This resulted in enhanced margins across the company," said chief executive David W. Johnson.
Net sales for the quarter were up three percent to a record $2.05 billion compared with $1.99 billion last year. Excluding divestitures, sales rose six percent for the quarter.

Net earnings, before special charges, increased 14 percent to $248 million from $219 million a year earlier. Earnings per share, before special charges, increased 15 percent to a quarterly record of $1.01 from $0.88.

"As we celebrate the 100th anniversary of condensed soup in 1997, brand innovations like premium soup in glass and new frozen soups will provide unprecedented opportunities to grow new channels and win consumers with products of superior quality, Johnson said.

As previously announced, a charge of $160 million was taken in the first quarter to cover the costs of restructuring, including plant closings, asset sales, divestitures and organizational changes. This reduced net earnings to $88 million and earnings per share to $0.36 for the quarter.
